paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the size of a dataset, denoted as |S|, and cosine similarity. The x-axis is labeled “|S|”, has a linear scale ranging from 2 to 10, and tick labels are placed at integer values. The y-axis is labeled “Cosine similarity”, has a linear scale ranging from 0.1 to 0.5, and tick labels are placed at intervals of 0.1. A blue, dashed line representing “Weight averaging” begins at approximately 0.42 when |S| is 2, decreases to 0.37 when |S| is 4, remains at approximately 0.34 from |S| = 6 to |S| = 8, and concludes at 0.31 when |S| is 10. A green line, labeled “QAdapter” and marked with circular data points and a dashed line style, starts at approximately 0.33 when |S| is 2, decreases to 0.27 when |S| is 4, continues to decline to 0.24 when |S| is 6, and then levels off at approximately 0.22 from |S| = 8 to |S| = 10.
